title: Measurement incompatibility and noiseless quantum codes
abstract: We construct a rank-one minimal informationally complete measurement (MIC) with an invertible dual operator and prove that, for arbitrary finite input and output dimensions, a channel universally preserves measurement incompatibility if and only if its input space contains a noiseless code subspace of the full output dimension. Preserving the compatibility threshold of a finite family of binary measurements already guarantees such a code. Furthermore, for every $d\ge2$, there exists a family of binary measurements that is incompatible on the full space but compatible after compression to any proper subspace. These results resolve the conjecture of Chitambar and Zhang and the existence question posed by Uola and coauthors. We also give an explicit construction of exact encodings and show that, for a sufficiently small shift in the compatibility threshold, the transmission error of an approximate encoding is bounded by a constant times the square of the shift. These results establish a connection between measurement compatibility, quantum steering, and quantum error correction.
summary: This theoretical paper establishes a fundamental equivalence: a quantum channel preserves measurement incompatibility if and only if the input space contains a noiseless code subspace. It resolves major open conjectures by connecting measurement compatibility directly to the requirements for quantum error correction, providing explicit constructions and error bounds.
main_problem: The paper investigates the necessary and sufficient conditions for a quantum channel to universally preserve the property of measurement incompatibility.
main_result: Universal preservation of measurement incompatibility is equivalent to the input space containing a noiseless code subspace of the full output dimension, resolving key conjectures in the field.
method: The authors use advanced concepts from quantum information theory, including constructing rank-one Minimal Informationally Complete Measurements (MICs) and relating incompatibility to quantum steering.
model_or_system: The study focuses on abstract quantum channels ($\Lambda: D 	o d$) acting on quantum states, analyzing the compatibility of finite families of quantum measurements.
key_observables: Measurement incompatibility/compatibility, noiseless code subspace existence, and the compatibility threshold.
important_parameters: The dimension of the input/output spaces ($D, d$), and the shift parameter ($\delta$) used in error bounding.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the mathematical framework of quantum channels and the properties of informationally complete measurements.
paper_structure: The paper builds by first reviewing the link between incompatibility and steering, proving the main equivalence theorem using MICs, and then providing explicit constructions and error bounds for approximate encodings.
why_interesting: It establishes a deep, quantitative link between fundamental concepts like measurement compatibility, quantum steering, and the existence of error-correcting codes, which is central to quantum information theory.
